messages:
carmen: Quick follow-up on the quota-harmonization RFC — we need to pick an interface for edge vs central enforcement. My summary: central admission gives consistent fairness but adds RTT/ops. Edge/local admission reduces RTT but diverges on state. Thoughts?
ben: I worry about split-brain fairness if edges have slightly stale budgets. Hard to reason about long-tail tenants.
amy: Agreed. Also telemetry: central admission gives a single decision point so we can emit neat per-tenant metrics. Edge decisions scatter telemetry across proxies.
ben: True, but central admission becomes a hot path. Can we make it async for best-effort fairness? e.g., admit locally then reconcile with central async? :thinking:
carmen: That was in the RFC (soft-admit + reconcile), but we need clearer contract around what "soft-admit" means. Should runtime ever serve more than X% above central budget before getting penalized?
sam: Proposal: admission service returns a tuple: (decision, lease_ttl, budget_hint). decision ∈ {ADMIT, PROBATION, REJECT}. If PROBATION, edge may serve up to budget_hint tokens or time window. Edge must attach `lease_id` to requests so central can reconcile.
amy: I like the explicit `lease_id`. Also add `reason_code` for observability: e.g., `REASON=abuse_score_high` vs `REASON=burst-probe`.
ben: Implementation detail: how do edges get budgets offline? If control plane down, edges should still operate in read-only fallback with conservative defaults. We should define a config param `edge_fallback_policy` = conservative|lenient|stop.
carmen: Good. Tradeoffs callout: conservative reduces availability for legitimate spikes; lenient increases abuse risk. Need product input for default.
sam: For abuse detection, should that live in admission or as a pre-filter at edge? Edge detectors get more signals (source IP, TLS info) quickly but are easier to evade. Central detectors have global view but higher latency. Hybrid seems needed: fast heuristics at edge (rate-of-change, entropy) + central ML scoring for correlated signals.
amy: Hybrid makes sense. How about interface for scores: edge sends a compact fingerprint + recent counters to central and central returns a normalized `abuse_score` 0..100 and suggested action. Keep fingerprint small: `sha256(user_id + short_salt)` or `flow_id`.
ben: We must be careful about PII. Use hashed IDs only, and document GDPR implications.
carmen: On quotas semantics: token-level vs request-level billing. Runtime cares about tokens, frontdoor cares about requests. Need to standardize a small protobuf: {request_tokens:int, response_tokens:int, cost_units:float}. Edge should compute `request_tokens` estimate and runtime returns exact after generation for reconciliation.
sam: Example header exchange: `X-Quota-Lease: lease_id=abc123;ttl=5s;hint=100tokens` and runtime returns `X-Quota-Actual: request=12;response=84;cost=0.096`.
amy: Also add `X-Quota-Trace: trace_id` for correlating. This will help debugging fair-shed cases.
ben: One more thing: fairness policies (per-tenant weight) — where should they live? If central only, edges need to be aware to avoid serving disproportionally. Suggest distributing compact policy blobs to edges with versioning: `policy_v:42`.
carmen: Agreed. Policy blobs + sequence numbers, with a simple last-write-wins. Edges can fall back to earlier policy if they lose connectivity.
sam: Performance note: central admission should be optimized for p99 < 5ms for small tokens; otherwise user-facing latency suffers. We can add local caching with TTL 500ms for repeated small clients.
amy: Ops: telemetry events to emit: admit_decision, lease_issued, probation_exceeded, reconciliation_delta. Each should include `policy_v`, `lease_id`, `abuse_score`.
carmen: Action items: 1) Ben to draft minimal protobufs for lease and reconciliation (due EOD Friday). 2) Amy to list telemetry events & fields. 3) Sam to spike a prototype `lease_id` header in proxy and measure added latency.
ben: I'll start the proto. Will ping infra channel once ready. :+1:
amy: I'll sketch telemetry. Low-cardinality keys first.
sam: I'll wire a quick header passthrough, can test with synthetic load.
ratebot: deploy-check: proxy-spike branch deployed to staging at commit abcdef; sampling enabled at 1% for now.
carmen: Thanks all — we'll reconvene next week after spikes.
